title: The Fox and the Leopard
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Fox and a Leopard were disputing about their looks, and each claimed to be the more handsome of the two. The Leopard said, "Look at my smart coat; you have nothing to match that." But the Fox replied, "Your coat may be smart, but my wits are smarter still."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what are the Fox and Leopard disputing about?
According to the passage, what does each of them claim to be?
options: The more handsome of the two

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Leopard tell the Fox to look at?
According to the passage, what does the Leopard say the Fox has nothing to match?
According to the passage, what does the Fox admit may be smart?
According to the passage, what does the Fox say is smarter still?
Based on the passage, why does the Fox admit the Leopard's coat 'may be smart' before answering?
options: Because he secretly wants a coat like the Leopard's
Because he no longer cares who is more handsome
Because he is trying to end the argument without a reply
To concede the point on looks before shifting the contest to wit, where he wins

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's reply suggest he values more than good looks?
As the passage uses it, what does "disputing" mean in "were disputing about their looks"?
Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Wit can outmatch mere good looks
Foxes and leopards should not argue
A fine coat guarantees respect from others

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who does the Fox argue with?
According to the passage, what did the Leopard say about his own coat?
options: That it was old and worn
To look at it, since the Fox had nothing to match it
That it was a gift from another animal
That he had never liked it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words does the Fox use about his wits?
options: "My wits are the sharpest of all"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is notable about how the Fox turns the Leopard's own word against him?
options: He reuses "smart" to mean clever instead of fine-looking
He insults the Leopard's appearance directly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Fox be satisfied with his answer even though he has no fine coat?
options: He plans to steal the Leopard's coat
He thinks the Leopard is lying about the coat
He has decided looks do not matter to leopards
He believes intelligence is worth more than appearance

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "wits" mean in "my wits are smarter still"?
Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Leopard defeats a Fox in a race and wins the argument
A Fox and Leopard agree they are equally handsome
A Fox and Leopard argue over who is more handsome, and the Fox claims his cleverness beats the Leopard's fine coat
A Leopard admits the Fox is smarter and more handsome
